## TL;DR

I ran a fixture-based QA pass on the Stories create, link and progress flows at 375, 768 and 1280 px. Two real gaps were fixed: the disabled Create story button gave no reason, and the duplicate-name error had no next step. A new headless WebKit suite covers create, duplicate name, server failure, unreachable server, zero-task and 40-task progress, and the story panel. The QA record is in `docs/qa/2026-11-story-flows-qa.md`. Linking and unlinking in a browser at each width are not verified. This handoff also fixes a flaky assertion in the sign-in QA suite (#1239) that failed the remote gate.

## Work and rationale

The task asked for an end-to-end QA pass with headless Playwright against fixtures, covering empty, many-task, duplicate-name and failure cases. I read the existing story code before writing tests. Creation goes through `NewStoryPanel.vue` and `POST /api/stories/freeform`. Linking is not a separate endpoint: a task carries a `story` tag, set from the Story select in the task drawer, and "No story" clears it. Progress is a roll-up from `mergeStoriesForDisplay` in `src/core/story-display.ts`, which returns 0% when a story has no tasks.

The server rejects duplicate names case-insensitively through `storyKey`, returning 409 with the reason text, and the UI `api()` helper surfaces that reason. The zero-task guard also held. Those paths were already correct, so the new tests are regression coverage rather than bug fixes.

The new suite, `src/ui-app/tests/stories-create-progress-qa-browser.test.ts`, follows the pattern of `stories-inbox-search-qa-browser.test.ts`. The real components mount in jsdom against seeded stores and stubbed `fetch`. The markup is then loaded into headless WebKit with the built stylesheet, and an audit checks for off-viewport elements, clipped controls and document width. It never opens a visible browser and makes no live-server calls.

Two product changes followed from the failures:

1. The Create story button is disabled until a description is entered, and nothing explained that. `NewStoryPanel.vue` now shows "Add a description to create the story." above the button row while the description is empty. The style is a small `.ff-hint` rule in `style.css`, next to `.ff-error`.
2. The duplicate-name message stated the conflict but gave no next step. `writeStoryDefinition` and `rewriteStoryDefinition` in `src/core/story-definition-files.ts` now end with "Choose a different name." The check itself is unchanged, and the 409 mapping in the route still matches on "already exists". I tightened the assertions in `story-definitions.test.ts` to check the full sentence.

I considered blocking duplicate names in the client before submit and set it aside. The server is the authority on names, including case-folded names and PM renames, and a client copy of that rule could drift.

## Approaches tried

My first run of the browser suite showed 15 failures, nearly all from the harness. Scoped CSS lookup failed for two components with no `<style>` block, so I dropped them from the scoped list, since their rules are global. The duplicate-name and failure tests then showed an empty error. `.click()` on the shared `Button` did not reach the handler under jsdom, so `fetch` was never called. I confirmed this with a temporary log in `createStory`, then reverted it. A native `dispatchEvent` click reached the handler. A second harness problem: typed input values are not part of `innerHTML`, so the WebKit page showed empty fields. I copied field values into attributes and text before capturing the markup.

The remaining suite failure after those fixes was the disabled-button hint, which was the product gap. It passes now.

## Challenges and blockers

The remote gate failure was in a different suite: `sign-in-users-qa-browser.test.ts` (#1239), "tells a locked-out visitor to wait". I could not reproduce it locally, and the stored remote output was not available to me, so I did not see the text the page showed. The test was the weak point. `textOf` returned as soon as the error element had any text, then asserted on it, so a transient message could fail the assertion. I changed `textOf` to take an optional expected matcher and wait until the text matches it. All assertion sites now pass the same matcher. Whether this is the exact cause on the thinkpad runner is unconfirmed. The change removes the race regardless.

Linking and unlinking are not fully verified at each width. The Story select lives in the task drawer, and the existing audit helpers do not mount the drawer. `task-drawer-story-select.test.ts` covers the new-task unlink, where "No story" clears the tag before create. The edit-drawer save path for link and unlink has no independent assertion. I recorded this as a gap in the QA doc rather than claiming coverage I did not measure. Closing it needs a drawer audit at 375 and 768 px, which is a bigger harness job.

I did not run a live server pass. The task is fixture-based, and a preview is a human's request.

One behavior is not changed. Registering a story whose name matches a tag-only story succeeds and merges into one group by name key, with no warning. That is a product decision, and the QA doc lists it as a follow-up.

## Key learnings

- A disabled control needs a visible reason, or it reads as broken. A state-based hint is the cheapest fix.
- Server copy that names a conflict should name the next step too. Keep the tests on the sentence, so the copy can change without breaking the regex matches.
- In jsdom-to-WebKit fixtures, anything not serialized into `innerHTML` is lost: input values, textarea state and listeners. A harness that copies markup must copy that state too.
- A text assertion should wait for the value it asserts, not for any text. Waiting for "non-empty" lets an earlier message win.

## Verification

- `bun run build` succeeded, which the browser suite needs for the built stylesheet.
- `bun run test:vitest` on six files (the new story browser suite, `story-definitions`, `stories-view`, `story-panel`, `stories-inbox-search-qa-browser`, and `sign-in-users-qa-browser`): 153 tests passed locally after the final edits.
- `bun run fmt` ran over the changed files.
- `repoos check --changed main` passed ("All checks passed"), including the rendered contrast audit and the UI smoke test. Its test step was skipped locally (`REPOOS_SKIP_TESTS=1`) and runs on the remote validation runner, so the six-file run above is the local test evidence.
